reference.source: Harrison's Principles of Internal Medicine / standard immunology references
clinicalPearls: Hyper-IgM syndrome is a group of disorders in which B cells cannot switch from producing IgM to other antibody classes, so IgM is normal or high while IgG, IgA, and IgE are low
The most common form is X-linked, caused by deficiency of CD40 ligand (CD40L/CD154) on activated T cells
The failure of the CD40-CD40L interaction impairs both class switching and germinal centre formation, and in the X-linked form also disrupts T-cell help to macrophages

Because of the combined defect, the X-linked form behaves like a combined immunodeficiency, with susceptibility to opportunistic organisms including Pneumocystis jirovecii and Cryptosporidium as well as pyogenic bacteria
Cryptosporidial infection is an important cause of sclerosing cholangitis and chronic diarrhoea in these patients
Neutropenia is a frequent accompanying feature, particularly in the CD40L-deficient form

Activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AID) deficiency causes an autosomal recessive form limited to B cells, presenting with pyogenic infections and lymphoid hyperplasia but without the opportunistic infection profile
Management includes immunoglobulin replacement, Pneumocystis prophylaxis, measures to avoid Cryptosporidium (safe water), and haematopoietic stem cell transplantation for the X-linked CD40L form
reference.pathophysiology: Hyper-IgM syndromes disrupt immunoglobulin class-switch recombination. In the X-linked form, mutations in the gene for CD40 ligand deprive B cells and antigen-presenting cells of the CD40 signal that activated T cells normally deliver, preventing class switching, germinal centre development, and effective T-cell-dependent activation of macrophages and dendritic cells. This dual impairment of humoral and cell-mediated immunity explains both the pyogenic infections and the opportunistic infections. Autosomal recessive forms caused by intrinsic B-cell defects, such as deficiency of activation-induced cytidine deaminase (AICDA) or uracil-DNA glycosylase, block the enzymatic machinery of switching within the B cell itself, producing a purely humoral phenotype with prominent lymphoid hyperplasia.
additionalDifferentials: Severe combined immunodeficiency (for the opportunistic infection picture)
Other combined immunodeficiencies with opportunistic infection
Secondary causes of low class-switched immunoglobulins
additionalInvestigations: Immunoglobulin panel showing normal or elevated IgM with low IgG and IgA
Flow cytometry for CD40L expression on activated T cells (X-linked form)
Genetic testing (CD40LG, CD40, AICDA, UNG among others)
Full blood count to detect neutropenia
Screening for Pneumocystis and Cryptosporidium in appropriate clinical settings
Liver function tests and imaging for sclerosing cholangitis
redFlags: Opportunistic infection such as Pneumocystis pneumonia requiring urgent treatment and prophylaxis
Cryptosporidial infection with chronic diarrhoea or evolving sclerosing cholangitis
Severe neutropenia predisposing to invasive infection
Live vaccines should be avoided in the combined X-linked form
Recurrent or severe infection in an infant boy warranting prompt immunological workup
reference.prognosis: The X-linked CD40L-deficient form has a serious prognosis because of opportunistic infections, liver disease from cryptosporidiosis, and an increased risk of malignancy, and haematopoietic stem cell transplantation is often recommended; the B-cell-intrinsic recessive forms generally have a better outlook managed with immunoglobulin replacement.
pitfalls: Assuming a normal or high IgM excludes significant immunodeficiency
Treating the X-linked form as a purely antibody deficiency and omitting Pneumocystis prophylaxis
Overlooking Cryptosporidium as a cause of chronic diarrhoea and liver disease
Failing to distinguish the combined X-linked form from the milder B-cell-intrinsic recessive forms, which affects prognosis and transplant decisions
management: Establish regular immunoglobulin replacement as the cornerstone of therapy to compensate for absent IgG and IgA
Start Pneumocystis prophylaxis with co-trimoxazole in the X-linked CD40 ligand-deficient form owing to the opportunistic infection risk
Reduce cryptosporidial exposure with boiled or filtered water and treat intercurrent bacterial infection promptly with targeted antibiotics
Refer for allogeneic haematopoietic stem cell transplantation, often recommended in CD40 ligand deficiency to prevent liver disease and malignancy
Support associated neutropenia with granulocyte colony-stimulating factor
Monitor liver function and screen for sclerosing cholangitis while remaining vigilant for malignancy
Provide genetic counselling for the family given X-linked inheritance, and manage care through clinical immunology
